questions.q: How does the lesson describe the relationship between application CI/CD from course 12 and CI/CD for models?
options: Model CI/CD is unrelated to application CI/CD and uses entirely different tooling concepts
The same pipeline discipline applies, but the 'commit' can be new data or a drift alert, the 'tests' are an evaluation gate, and the 'deployment' is a registry promotion
Model CI/CD never uses pipelines at all; it is always a manual process
Application CI/CD pipelines automatically handle model training without any changes
questions.explain: The core shape is the same pipeline discipline from course 12, just applied to a model artifact: triggers, automated checks, and automated promotion, with model-specific equivalents for each piece.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a real trigger for an automated retraining pipeline?
options: Only a manual click from a data scientist, with no other trigger type possible
A change to the company's marketing website
The GPU driver version being updated on the training cluster
A scheduled run, a drift alert from the monitoring system, or a change to the training code/config
questions.explain: The lesson names three triggers: scheduled retraining on a fixed cadence, drift-triggered retraining fired by a monitoring alert, and a push-triggered retrain from a training code or config change.

questions.q: What does an automated evaluation gate do inside a model CI/CD pipeline?
options: It skips evaluation entirely to save compute time
It always promotes the new model regardless of its metrics
It compares the new model's metrics against the current production model's metrics (from the registry) and fails the pipeline if the new model doesn't clear the bar
It only checks that the training script has no syntax errors
questions.explain: The gate pulls the current production model's metrics from the registry and compares them against the new model's metrics, stopping the pipeline if the new model doesn't beat or match that bar.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a failed evaluation gate is 'a sign the system is working, not broken'?
options: Because most retraining runs will not beat the current production model, and the gate's job is preventing a worse model from being shipped automatically
Because pipelines are expected to fail most of the time regardless of model quality
Because a failed gate means the registry itself is corrupted
Because evaluation gates are purely cosmetic and have no real effect on deployment
questions.explain: A failed gate means the pipeline correctly blocked a model that didn't clear the bar from being promoted — exactly the safety check the gate exists to provide.

questions.q: What happens when a retrained model clears the evaluation gate, according to this lesson?
options: A data scientist must still manually run the promotion command before anything changes
The pipeline's final step promotes the model in the registry automatically, the same way GitOps reconciliation handles application deployments without a manual production change
The model is deleted and training starts over from scratch
Nothing happens until the next scheduled retraining run begins
questions.explain: A passing gate triggers an automated promotion step in the registry — the model equivalent of GitOps reconciliation, where the desired state is reached without a manual production action.
